configuration.title: Markdown Editor for Humans
configuration.imagePath.description: Folder path for saved images. Interpreted relative to markdownForHumans.imagePathBase.
configuration.imagePathBase.description: Controls whether Image Path is relative to the current markdown file folder or the workspace folder.
configuration.chromePath.markdownDescrip:
Path to Google Chrome or Chromium executable for PDF export. Leave empty to auto-detect.

**Download Chrome:**
- [Windows/Mac/Linux](https://www.google.com/chrome/)
- [Chromium (open source)](https://www.chromium.org/getting-involved/download-chromium/)

**Common paths:**
- **Mac:** `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome`
- **Windows:** `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`
- **Linux:** `/usr/bin/google-chrome` or `/usr/bin/chromium`
configuration.imageResize.skipWarning.de: Skip the warning dialog when resizing images. When enabled, images will be resized immediately without confirmation.
configuration.feedback.handoffPromptTemp: Prompt copied after a feedback bundle is sealed. `{{feedbackFile}}` is required and expands as Markdown inline code. Optional placeholders are `{{source}}` (also Markdown inline code), `{{sourceSha256}}`, `{{itemCount}}`, and `{{round}}`. Invalid or oversized templates safely fall back to this built-in prompt.
configuration.blankLines.mode.descriptio: Controls whether extra blank lines are preserved or removed in the editor and saved file.
configuration.imagePreview.hover.enabled: Enable the image hover overlay that shades images and displays metadata (resolution, file size, etc.) on hover.
configuration.paragraph.spacingBefore.de: Space before paragraphs in points (margin-top). Default: 0pt
configuration.paragraph.spacingAfter.des: Space after paragraphs in points (margin-bottom). Default: 0pt
configuration.zoom.description: Zoom level for the editor as a percentage. 100 = default size, 150 = 50% larger, etc.
configuration.font.family.markdownDescri:
Font for body text and headings. Use any font installed on your computer; separate several with commas and the first one found is used. Leave empty for the standard font. Example: `Atkinson Hyperlegible, sans-serif`

Code stays monospace, and math and diagrams keep their own fonts. If a font is not installed, the standard font is used. PDF and Word exports keep their own fonts.
configuration.font.weight.markdownDescri:
Weight of body text, from 100 (thin) to 900 (heavy). 400 is normal. Example: `500` for slightly heavier text.

Your font must include the weight you choose. Headings and bold text keep their own weight.
configuration.font.lineHeight.markdownDe:
Line height of body text, as a multiple of the font size. Example: `1.8` for more room between lines.

Applies to paragraphs, lists, tables, quotes and alerts. Headings and code keep their own line height.
configuration.font.letterSpacing.markdow:
Extra space between letters, as a fraction of the font size. 0 keeps the standard spacing. Example: `0.05` for slightly wider letters.

Applies to body text and headings. Code and math are not changed.
configuration.font.wordSpacing.markdownD:
Extra space between words, as a fraction of the font size. 0 keeps the standard spacing. Example: `0.16` to set words further apart, which helps when letter spacing is raised.

Applies to body text and headings. Code and math are not changed.
configuration.font.useEditorFont.markdow:
Use your VS Code editor font for body text: `editor.fontFamily`, `editor.fontWeight` and `editor.fontSize`, including values set under `"[markdown]"` in settings.json. The VS Code default editor font is monospace, so turn this on only if you have set an editor font you like to read in.

`#markdownForHumans.font.family#` and `#markdownForHumans.font.weight#` take priority when you change them.
configuration.enableMath.description: Render LaTeX math expressions using KaTeX. Use $...$ for inline math and $$...$$ for display math. Toggling this setting requires reopening the editor.
configuration.formattingShortcuts.enable: When enabled, Cmd/Ctrl+B, +I, and +U toggle bold/italic/underline inside the editor. Disable this if you rely on VS Code keybindings that use the same chords (e.g. a sidebar toggle rebound to Cmd+B) and want them to keep working while a markdown file is open in this editor.
